The '''Premier League Young Player of the Season''' is an annual English [[association football|football]] award, presented to the best player aged 23 or younger in the [[Premier League]]. For sponsorship purposes, it is known as the '''[[Hublot]] Young Player of the Season''' since the [[2020–21 Premier League|2020–21 season]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1814342|publisher=Premier League |date=9 September 2020|access-date=6 May 2021|title=Hublot to be Premier League's official timekeeper}}</ref> after being known as '''[[TAG Heuer]] Young Player of the Season''' right after its inception during the [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1419796|publisher=Premier League |date=10 October 2019|access-date=7 August 2020 |title=TAG Heuer Young Player of the Season award launched}}</ref>

[[Trent Alexander-Arnold]] of [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] was the first winner of the award.<ref name="TAA20"/> [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] player [[Phil Foden]] has won the most awards with two.<ref name="PF47"/> In 2024, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] midfielder [[Cole Palmer]] became the first player to receive the award while not winning the league.<ref name="Palmer24">{{Cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4010760|date=17 May 2024|publisher=Premier League|access-date=17 May 2024|title= Palmer wins Hublot Young Player of the Season award}}</ref> The current holder of the award is Manchester City full-back [[Nico O'Reilly]].<ref name="O'Reilly"/>
